The capability architecture

Alterac Valley's Weather

One sky for every match, and a storm that wanders it

Rules and Viewsplanned; this page is the plan, and the simulator is built once the owner approves it

The owner, 2026-10-29: "Can we make issue files for a feature where the Alterac Valleys on the server all share the same weather? And it oscillates in a pattern (is collages) that is non deterministic yet still equally distributed. A storm cloud should wander across the map and always be intensely downpowering"

One sky

Every Alterac Valley match on the server shows the same weather at the same moment: one clock for the whole server. A match that opens, and a player who arrives in one, is given the weather of that moment. It sits behind a switch, Buddies.AlteracWeather, off until turned on.

The deck

The weather kinds are dealt like a shuffled deck: fine, fog, light snow, snow, heavy snow, light slush and slush. Each kind comes once a deck, in a fresh random order each time, from a seed nobody can predict. Over any whole number of decks every kind has had exactly the same time: that is the "non deterministic yet still equally distributed". A new deck never opens with the kind the last one closed on. Each turn lasts six minutes, swelling from nothing to full and fading back.

Slush

The owner: "the rain freezes to slush." The game has no sleet, so a slush turn is drawn from rain and snow: it opens as rain, trades back and forth between rain and snow through its middle, and closes as snow.

The storm

One storm cell, the same in every match, drifts at a walking pace, two yards a second. It keeps its heading for a while and turns gently, turning back from the valley's edges. Within 60 yards of it everyone is in the heaviest rain the game shows, with thunder, always; from 60 to 90 yards it fades into the shared sky. The game sends weather for a whole zone at once, so the storm is drawn by sending each player under it their own weather.

Even over time

The storm leans toward the parts of the valley it has visited least lately, so over a long match every part has had its share. The same idea as the deck, in space: unpredictable from moment to moment, even over time.

What is built once approved

A simulator: the deck dealt on a timeline with each turn's swell and fade, slush turns trading rain and snow, and the storm wandering the real valley map with a heat map of where it has been, with sliders for turn length, storm size and pace.
